title: The Barrens
body: The Barrens is a vast savanna of red earth, yellow grass and thorny scrub in the heart of Kalimdor, stretching from the forests of Ashenvale in the north to the canyons of Thousand Needles in the south, with Durotar across the river to the east and Mulgore beyond the hills to the west. Long ago it was woodland tended by the night elves, until the Burning Legion, war and the Sundering left it scorched and dry. In recent years new oases have formed, fed by some power seeping up from below, and the life they bring is not wholly natural. The Horde holds the Crossroads where the great roads meet, the tauren keep Camp Taurajo, and orc posts watch the borders at Far Watch and Mor'shan. Kolkar centaurs, Razormane and Bristleback quilboar and Witchwing harpies all contest the land. Goblins run the free port of Ratchet while the Venture Company drills in the north, Theramore's soldiers hold Northwatch on the coast, dwarves dig at Bael Modan, and silithid swarm in the Field of Giants.

title: Far Watch Post
body: Far Watch Post is the orc garrison that guards the Barrens end of the bridge over the Southfury River, the first stop on the western road out of Razor Hill. Kargal Battlescar commands it, signing the letters of young conscripts sent over from Durotar and passing them on to the Crossroads, where, he grumbles, the real need lies. Two others keep company with him. Ak'Zeloth, assistant to the warlock Neeru Fireblade of Orgrimmar, keeps a table of flawed power stones close at hand, readied for a task on Dreadmist Peak, and just to the south the veteran Uzzek, a fighter of many battles, drills young warriors in the art of defense.

title: Dreadmist Peak
body: Dreadmist Peak rises from the plains north of the Crossroads, and the safest way to its summit lies up the northern face. Cultists of the Burning Blade have made it their own. Bruisers and acolytes of the cult guard its slopes, and among them, seldom seen, walks Rathorian, a felguard demon. In a cave near the top, the Dreadmist Den, the Demon Seed rests above a demonic altar of fire: an object of power around which the cult rallies, and a tool of the Burning Legion itself. Not every tenant of the peak belongs to the cult. An undead mage, Sarilus Foulborne, keeps to the heights alone.

title: Grol'dom Farm
body: Grol'dom Farm is a small orc homestead north of the Crossroads, on the road that leads toward the night elf forests. It is a family place. Karu cooks roasted plainstrider over the fire and wonders why the pigs were never fed, Trok runs in circles trying to escape a swarm of angry bees, and young Okla begs her father for leave to gather pretty stones for a necklace, with a sharp one saved for her friend Gruk's spear. Her father is Kranal Fiss, and he is more than a farmer. Young shamans of the Horde are sent to his door when they are ready to learn the ways of fire.

title: Thorn Hill
body: Northeast of the Crossroads, where great thorny vines thrust up out of the earth, the Razormane quilboar have dug their dens. The thorns mark the quilboar wherever they settle, and from Thorn Hill the Razormane strike at the caravans that carry supplies along the road from Durotar, leaving stolen crates of the Crossroads' goods strewn through their camps. Water seekers, thornweavers, geomancers and defenders crowd the hill under the eye of Elder Mystic Razorsnout, and the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout leads the attacks. They have not spared the hermit smith on the hills nearby either: an iron chest stolen from his camp lies among their huts.

title: The Crossroads
body: The Crossroads is the largest Horde town in the Barrens, a walled outpost raised where the great roads of the Barrens cross. Thork leads its defenses in the Warchief's name, and the shaman Sergra Darkthorn sets newcomers to work. Raids on its caravans keep the garrison busy, and the town is full of tasks: Darsok Swiftdagger wants harpies dead, Gazrog wants back the guards' silver payroll, stolen by raptors of all things, and the troll Korran studies the strange insects of the south for his masters in Orgrimmar. The Forsaken apothecary Helbrim works among the tents, the druid Tonga Runetotem ponders the oases, and the grieving warrior Mankrik watches the horizon from dawn till dusk.

title: The Dry Hills
body: The Dry Hills climb toward the mountains in the northwest of the Barrens, and they belong to the Witchwing harpies. The harpies are not native to these plains: they came down from Stonetalon, far to the northwest, and they have been ravaging the Horde's caravan supplies for a long time. Their flock keeps a strict order. Harpies and roguefeathers make up the lower ranks, windcallers and ambushers fly among them, and the slayers serve as lieutenants, each marked by a ring she carries. Above them all is Serena Bloodfeather, whose raids are revenge for a sister slain by Rexxar, and a harpy called Sister Rathtalon is sometimes seen hunting the hills.

title: The Forgotten Pools
body: Northwest of the Crossroads lie the Forgotten Pools, one of the oases that have formed in the Barrens in recent years. Deep beneath their waters is a fissure in the earth, gases bubbling up from it, and the druid Tonga Runetotem believes it may be the very source of the life now stirring in this dry land. That life has its oddities. Laden mushrooms grow by the water, their spores prized by the apothecaries of the Forsaken, and strange deviate fish swim in the pools. Kolkar centaurs, wranglers and stormers, keep camp along the banks, and the Kolkar leader Barak Kodobane has made his camp near the pools.

title: The Mor'shan Rampart
body: In the far north of the Barrens, where the grass gives way to the forests of Ashenvale, the Horde has raised the Mor'shan Rampart, a fortified wall and watch tower to hold the border against the night elves. Barrens guards keep the gate. Kadrak commands from the tower and leads the Horde's campaign in Ashenvale, sending fresh recruits on to the new outposts at Splintertree and the Zoram Strand and runners with fresh orders to his Warsong scouts. He will not suffer Alliance messengers to cross Horde ground. Just to the south, the goblin tinkerer Wenikee Boltbucket keeps a camp, ready to take apart any machine that catches her eye.

title: The Sludge Fen
body: The Sludge Fen is a fouled stretch of the northern Barrens where the Venture Company works its derricks. Drudgers and mercenaries swarm the site under Supervisor Lugwizzle, shredders lumber about, and tool buckets lie everywhere, stocked with the company's nugget slugs. The rivals of Ratchet watch it closely: one goblin spy climbed into a stolen shredder here only to find he had no key. North of the fen stands a Venture Co. tower, southwest of it a small research site guards a device called the samophlange, and to the northeast the company's Boulder Lode Mine is worked by overseers and enforcers, where a miner is rumored to have dug up an emerald the size of a fist.

title: Ratchet
body: Ratchet is the goblin port on the eastern coast of the Barrens, founded by Gazlowe with the pay Thrall gave him for building Orgrimmar. It is a town of the Steamwheedle Cartel and open to all who trade in peace, and the boat Maiden's Fancy carries its cargo and passengers across the sea to Booty Bay. Everyone here has a scheme. Wharfmaster Dizzywig keeps the ledgers of every crate, Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union runs a shredder program, Mebok Mizzyrix brews smart drinks, Brewmaster Drohn keeps the old recipes of Chen Stormstout, and the high elf Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers. A small coven of warlocks makes its home here too.

title: The Tidus Stair
body: Along the shore south of Ratchet, beyond the mouth of the Southfury, the tauren shaman Islen Waterseer keeps a fishing hut. She is a teacher of water. Young shamans of the Horde are sent to her when their spirits are warmed by fire, and even outsiders come seeking her friendship with the spirits of water: a corrupted moon well's water was once carried to her from Felwood, and she asked the spirits themselves whether the cause was just. Beside her camps Mahren Skyseer, sister of Jorn of Camp Taurajo, who hunts the great beasts of the sea along this coast and takes on any hunter her brother has judged worthy.

title: The Merchant Coast
body: South of Ratchet the shore runs on as the Merchant Coast, and the trade it was named for now has to sail past pirates. The Southsea Freebooters have set up a camp here, almost on Gazlowe's doorstep, and their brigands and cannoneers guard strongboxes full of plunder taken from goblin ships: crates of boots from Booty Bay, a lens for Gazlowe's observatory and other stolen goods lie among their tents. Their captain, Baron Longshore of Gilneas, commands the ship called the Heedless and has a price on his head. Their ship, the Tide Razor, lies along this coast too, with a den aboard where they train their thieves, and makrura and sand sharks haunt the shallows.

title: Fray Island
body: Fray Island lies off the Merchant Coast, reached by wading the sand bar shallows, and it is a place where warriors meet to fight one another. Its chief warrior is the human Klannoc Macleod, called the Islander, who welcomes rising fighters of any people. Those who want his teaching must first pass the Affray. At its heart the challenger steps onto a grate before a crowd of cheering spectators, and the goblin announcer Twiggy Flathead calls out challenger after challenger, until at last he sends in Big Will. Only one who beats them all in the time allowed earns Klannoc's respect, and with it the berserker's way.

title: Northwatch Hold
body: Northwatch Hold is a human fortress on the coast south of Ratchet, built by survivors of the Alliance expedition and held now by marines and preservers of Theramore, blocking the coastal road toward Dustwallow Marsh. Captain Fairmount commands it with her cannoneers Whessan and Smythe, and their guns have sunk so many ships that Captain Brightsun of Ratchet calls them overzealous, trigger happy louts. They hold at least one prisoner: Gilthares Firebough, a deckhand on a moonshine run who was branded a threat to the Alliance. The waters offshore belong to Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, a sea beast the humans on this coast have every reason to fear.

title: Lushwater Oasis
body: Lushwater Oasis lies south of the Crossroads, one of the green pools that have sprung up across the plains, and beneath it opens the mouth of the Wailing Caverns. The druid Naralex went down into those caverns hoping to dream the Barrens green again, and his dream turned to nightmare. His few faithful disciples keep watch near the entrance, asking travelers to cull the deviate beasts that crawl from below. Above ground the oasis belongs to the Kolkar. Hezrul Bloodmark, leader of all the Kolkar centaurs in the Barrens, commands his people from here and berates them to look fierce, while snapjaw turtles altered by the water lurk at the shore.

title: The Stagnant Oasis
body: Southeast of the Crossroads lies the Stagnant Oasis, its waters as still as its name. The Kolkar have pitched a command tent here, and bloodchargers, marauders and pack runners with their hounds guard it, alongside two notorious brutes, Brokespear and Rocklance. The dervish Verog wanders the plains from this camp, and when the centaurs are pressed hard enough they raise an alarm and he comes, calling challengers to his tent to die. Beneath the water lies another bubbling fissure: dead and dried seeds dropped into it sprang to life, a sign that whatever rises from below can make life from nothing. Sunscale raptors nest to the southwest.

title: Camp Taurajo
body: Camp Taurajo is the tauren outpost of the southern Barrens, standing on the road east from Mulgore where young tauren first come down from their homeland. Kirge Sternhorn senses a foul wind blowing from the east, and he sends the newly arrived north to the Crossroads, for the lives of the tauren and the orcs are now intertwined. The hunter Jorn Skyseer guides those who walk his path, Ruga Ragetotem sets warriors a trial among the silithid, and the orc smith Tatternack Steelforge studies the crude weapons of the quilboar for the Warchief. The camp's strangest resident is a prisoner: the caged Razormane Mangletooth, who has information to sell.

title: Agama'gor and Bramblescar
body: North of Camp Taurajo, giant thorns burst from the earth at Agama'gor and Bramblescar, and here the Bristleback quilboar keep their camps. To the quilboar such thorns are holy, for they grew where the blood of their boar god Agamaggan fell, and the Bristlebacks dig blood red shards from the ground among them to carry as totems of strength and magic. Hunters and water seekers fill the camps, while thornweavers and geomancers gather at Bramblescar. The Bristlebacks are bitter rivals of the Razormane, and bitter enemies of the Horde: an orc grunt named Dogran was taken captive at Agama'gor after a raid on their huts went wrong.

title: Field of Giants
body: South of Camp Taurajo spreads the Field of Giants, where great mounds of earth rise from the grass and something has come that does not belong. Silithid have made their hives here: creepers, swarmers and grubs pour from the mounds, and a huge harvester stalks among them. The insects are new to the Barrens, and those who watch them are uneasy. They show more wit than any beast should, Korran of the Crossroads thinks, and his reports have reached Orgrimmar. Ruga Ragetotem dislikes what they herald, and Jorn Skyseer, holding the harvester's head, fears it may foretell a grim future for his people.

title: Blackthorn Ridge
body: Blackthorn Ridge lies deep in the south of the Barrens, beyond the Field of Giants, and it is Razormane country. Seers, stalkers, pathfinders and warfrenzied warriors of the tribe crowd its thorny slopes, and their weapons are better made than anyone expected of quilboar. From here the Razormane Nak, Kuz and Lok Orcbane, a caster, a tracker and a warrior who came out of the Kraul, direct the raids that trouble the north, and a brute named Hagg Taurenbane prowls among them. Yet someone lives here by choice: the orc shaman Brine keeps a lonely hut on the ridge, beside a watering hole the quilboar guard like treasure.

title: Bael Modan
body: South of the Field of Giants, the dwarves of Ironforge have torn open the earth at Bael Modan. Excavators and foremen blast deep holes into the ground with explosives and noisy machines, a flying machine stands over the dig, and the fortress of Bael'dun Keep, built to guard the site, now bristles with riflemen, soldiers and officers under General Twinbraid. The land was not empty. Tauren of the Stonespire tribe once lived here, and many were killed or driven off when the dwarves came. The dig's first great find, a gem called the Tear of the Moons, was locked away as cursed after it drove the dwarf Feegly mad.

title: The Razorfen
body: In the far south of the Barrens, near the edge of the Thousand Needles, rise the Razorfen, the greatest of all the thorn clusters. The quilboar hold that they are the very body of Agamaggan, their boar god, who fell in the War of the Ancients, and that the entrance to the Razorfen Downs is his great maw, which swallows any who are disloyal to him. In Razorfen Kraul the crone Charlga Razorflank musters a foul army, and the tauren Auld Stonespire of Thunder Bluff wants her heart for driving his people from their holy land. At the Downs a night elf watcher has seen something worse: an undead diplomat granting undeath to quilboar who beg for power.

title: Thork
body: Thork is the orc who leads the defenses of the Crossroads in the Warchief's name, and he welcomes newcomers so long as they mind their business. He has plenty to defend against. Razormane raids on the caravans from Durotar starve the town of supplies, and he sets the young to thin the quilboar, kill the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout and recover what was stolen. He was sure another quilboar led the raids, and was struck speechless when Lok Orcbane's skull was laid before him. Thork greets tauren sent from Camp Taurajo as allies and points eager recruits north to the Ashenvale front, but grieving Mankrik he turns away, saying rage clouds his judgment.

title: Sergra Darkthorn
body: Sergra Darkthorn is the orc shaman in charge of the Crossroads, and she makes it plain that she tolerates no insolence: Thrall himself, she reminds the young, has set the Horde's women on equal footing with its men. Kargal Battlescar of Far Watch grumbles that she will talk a recruit's head in circles, though Thrall is convinced she is something special. To young hunters she is a first guide, sending them after plainstriders, zhevra, prowlers and the great white cat Echeyakee. She teaches that there is more to hunting than killing, and when she sets them to defile the scytheclaw nests, she bids them ponder the lives of the beasts they slaughter.

title: Gazlowe
body: Gazlowe is the goblin who rules Ratchet. A goblin of Undermine and a member of the Steamwheedle Cartel, he served Thrall as chief engineer of Durotar, and with the gold the Warchief paid him for Orgrimmar he founded his own port in the Barrens. He keeps it open to anyone with coin and on good terms with the Horde. Business would be perfect but for the Southsea Freebooters, who raid his ships, camp on his doorstep and have stolen everything from his boots to the lens for his observatory, and he complains that the trade princes' fleets do too little about it. He has put a bounty on the head of their captain, Baron Longshore.

title: Mankrik
body: Mankrik is an orc warrior who came north to the Crossroads seeking help and found, he says, only cowards who turn their backs on him. He and his wife were fighting the Bristleback quilboar at a small tauren camp when the two were separated. She held three of them off alone, but more came, and when he turned in rage to face them, he was overwhelmed. A tauren druid found him lying on the Gold Road and tended his wounds. Now he stands at the Crossroads from sunrise to sunset scanning the horizon, killing every quilboar he meets and asking for their tusks. The body of his wife was found in the south, slain in battle.

title: Mangletooth
body: Mangletooth is a Razormane quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, and he is sure he will not leave it alive. His own tribe has abandoned him there to rot. Rather than forgive them, he trades in their secrets, offering the Horde the names of the Razormane who lead the raids on the Crossroads in return for blows against the Bristlebacks, the rival tribe he hates. He tells of Agamaggan, whose blood raised the thorns of the Barrens, and he still knows the old quilboar magic: bring him the blood shards the Bristlebacks carry, and he will bless the bearer with the boar god's strength, speed or spirit.

title: Jorn Skyseer
body: Jorn Skyseer is the tauren hunter of Camp Taurajo who teaches that, though others call this land barren, it teems with life for one who knows where to look. He takes up the training of young hunters after Sergra Darkthorn, and each beast he sets before them carries its own lesson: the savage Ishamuhale, the thunder lizards, the thunderhawk. To those who bring him tokens of legendary beasts like Lakota'mani the Earthshaker or Washte Pawne, he explains their meaning: Washte Pawne teaches that regret turns to wisdom. When a pupil has learned all he can teach, he sends them on: to his sister Mahren on the coast, to Ashenvale, or to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff.

title: Gann Stonespire
body: Gann Stonespire is a tauren who walks the southern Gold Road alone, seeking ways to defend his honor. His tribe once lived on the land the dwarves now tear apart at Bael Modan, and many of his people died or were driven from their birthplace when the excavation came. He tried to reach a peaceful resolution and failed. Now he wants the dwarves driven off by force, the journal of their prospector Khazgorm in his hands, and their own explosives turned against them: from Khazgorm's plans he fashions a charge to blow up the flying machine at the dig, which to him is an insult to the memory of his tribe.

title: Thun'grim Firegaze
body: Thun'grim Firegaze is an orc blacksmith of renown who lives as a hermit on a hilltop east of the Crossroads. His eyes have long dried out from staring into the forge's flame, and the Razormane took advantage of it: a few distracted him with snorts while others carried off his iron chest of forged steel bars. Warriors of the Horde seek him out for his weapons, and for those whose deeds have grown famous he will forge a suit of brutal armor, a labor so great that he wrote out the materials on a scroll over many nights with his failing eyes and calls on other smiths of the Horde to help.

title: Mebok Mizzyrix
body: Mebok Mizzyrix is a goblin of Ratchet who is always one deal away from a fortune. Convinced the raptors of the Barrens are smarter than most, he ground their horns into a smart drink, tasted it and found it terrible. Undaunted, he turned to the wailing essence of the caverns to the west, which he suspects is behind the strange plants and beasts of the land. His other ventures range wider: deepmoss spider eggs from Stonetalon for the omelette craze in Booty Bay, blueleaf tubers sniffed out by trained gophers in Razorfen Kraul, and bogbean leaves from the Dustwallow swamps, fetched by his hired help Stinky Ignatz.

title: Serena Bloodfeather
body: Serena Bloodfeather leads the Witchwing harpies of the Dry Hills, and her war on the Horde is a blood feud. Years ago the wanderer Rexxar, with the troll Rokhan beside him, killed her sister Bloodfeather, and Serena has answered by sending her flock against the Horde's caravans again and again. Darsok Swiftdagger of the Crossroads means to break her harpies from the bottom up, lieutenants first and the matriarch last, and to set her head on the next caravan he sends out as a warning to the rest. To the witch doctor Jin'Zil of Stonetalon, her death means the last of the Bloodfeathers is gone.

title: Grunt Dogran
body: Grunt Dogran was proud of his promotion to the Barrens, and his young mate Zankaja hid her worry when he left Orgrimmar. Stationed at Camp Taurajo, he led a few grunts against a Bristleback camp and was badly hurt and taken captive, and his wounds festered while the camp waited for a healing draught from the trolls of Malaka'jin. When help at last reached him, the draught gave him strength enough to hobble, but not to save his leg or his arm. He would not chain Zankaja to an invalid. He chose to seek an end in glorious battle instead, gave up a dirt-caked pendant, and asked that she never be told.

title: The Demon Seed
body: Hunting the Burning Blade through Durotar, the Horde learned from the warlock Neeru Fireblade that the cult rallies around an object of demonic power, the Demon Seed, kept atop Dreadmist Peak in the Barrens. Neeru, who claims to have searched out demonic corruption among the orcs since the last great war, wanted it destroyed, and sent the hero to his assistant Ak'Zeloth at Far Watch Post. Ak'Zeloth found the order strange, but he obeyed. He had prepared power stones to sever the Seed's link to the Legion, flawed things whose strength would burn itself out in time. Carried in haste up the northern face, past the cultists, and set at the altar of fire, a stone did its work. The Seed was destroyed, and Ak'Zeloth felt waves of staggering force pass through the ether, waves he was sure other beings had felt as well. Others, he warned, would wonder why their toy had been broken. Then he paid the hero, with Neeru's thanks.

title: Kranal Fiss and the Call of Fire
body: When a young orc, troll or tauren shaman has learned patience in the ways of earth, the trainers of Razor Hill, Orgrimmar, Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff send them north of the Crossroads to Kranal Fiss at Grol'dom Farm. He sees the burning desire in their eyes and warns them that power and destruction will come easily, but they must still know when to stay their hand. Then he gives them a torch to carry to the keeper of the Shrine of the Dormant Flame in Durotar. The fire sapta asks for fire tar, carried by the Razormane spellcasters of the eastern Barrens, and a reagent pouch taken from the Burning Blade, for a sapta is always made from things bound to its element. Fire is not only chaos and destruction, the keeper teaches, but life and creation, each force giving the other meaning. When the torch comes back lit from the shrine, Kranal sees a spirit that burns brighter than any torch, and presents the novice's first fire totem.

title: Islen Waterseer and the Call of Water
body: Shamans of the Horde whose spirits are warmed by fire are sent to Islen Waterseer at her fishing hut south of Ratchet. Her lesson is simple: water means rebirth, but polluted water devastates all it touches. For the sapta she sends them deep into the south to the shaman Brine, who lives alone on Blackthorn Ridge among hostile quilboar. Brine asks for three samples of the purest water: from the pond below her hut, which the quilboar guard as a sacred hoard, from a fresh well in the Forsaken town of Tarren Mill, a holy vestige in an unhallowed sea, and from the fountain at the Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. From them she makes a vial of purest water. Islen brews the sapta from it and sends the novice to a plague tainted shrine on the coast of Silverpine, where a corrupt manifestation of water must be defeated and a pure spirit called back. Water is life, the spirit says, and corruption stops life. Islen then gives the novice a water totem.

title: The Oases of the Barrens
body: The druids of Thunder Bluff sensed a strange power leaking into the Barrens, and Tonga Runetotem was sent to the Crossroads to find its source. Once lush, the land had been scorched to a husk by war and upheaval, yet in recent years new oases had formed and life was stirring. At the Forgotten Pools a fissure was found bubbling beneath the water. At the Stagnant Oasis dead, dried seeds dropped into another fissure sprang to life. But the snapjaw turtles of the oases bore a taint Tonga had never seen, as if the land dreamed and could not wake, and he named the Wailing Caverns its source. A shell went to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine, and the hero went on to the elder druids of Thunder Bluff, whose dreaming named the culprits: the Druids of the Fang, once part of a noble order that meant to heal the Barrens, now bent on remaking it to match their own twisted dreams. Their four leaders, Cobrahn, Anacondra, Pythas and Serpentis, each held a dream gem deep in the caverns.

title: The Kolkar Leaders
body: The Kolkar centaurs have long plagued the tauren, but in the Barrens they were disorganized, until new leaders rose to rally them. From his bunkers west of the Crossroads, Regthar Deathgate set out to destroy them one by one, and to pay bounties on every centaur bracer brought in. First fell Barak Kodobane, who camped near the Forgotten Pools. Then Verog the Dervish, who roams the plains, was drawn out by an attack on the command tent at the Stagnant Oasis until the alarm brought him charging in. Last was Hezrul Bloodmark, leader of all the Kolkar in the Barrens, cut down at Lushwater Oasis. The Kolkar answered in fury. A war band came out of Desolace, their homeland, to fall upon Regthar's bunkers from the west, and only when their warlord Krom'zar was slain and his banner taken did the attack break. Regthar promised that Thrall would hear of it, and he began to recruit for a campaign into Desolace itself.

title: The Hunt of the Barrens
body: Young hunters come to the Crossroads to learn that there is more to the hunt than finding and killing. Sergra Darkthorn starts them on plainstriders and zhevra, then the sly prowlers of the tall grass, and then Echeyakee, Whitemist, king of the savannah cats, called to his lair among the kodo bones with a horn; the tauren say he is both mercy and death. Next she has them leave raptor feathers on the scytheclaw nests, and asks them to ponder the lives they take. Then she sends them to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. Jorn sets them on Ishamuhale, Speartooth, the fiercest sunscale raptor, lured to a dead tree with a zhevra carcass, then on thunder lizards and the thunderhawk. A true hunter, Jorn teaches, can stalk prey down any path, even into the sea, and so he sends them to his sister Mahren on the coast, who sets them after Isha Awak, the Deep Doom, lord of the waters off Northwatch.

title: Betrayal from Within
body: Razormane raids on the caravans from Durotar were starving the Crossroads, and Thork wanted them stopped. His scouts named the raider Kreenig Snarlsnout, and Kreenig died, but he was not the true leader. The truth came from an unlikely mouth. In a cage at Camp Taurajo sat Mangletooth, a Razormane left to rot there by his own tribe. He offered a bargain: weaken the Bristlebacks, the Razormane's rivals, by killing their spiritual leaders, and he would tell who really led the raids. Then he told of Agamaggan, the boar god whose blood raised the thorns, and of the blood shards the Bristlebacks dig from the earth. At last he gave up his own kin. Three Razormane had come out of the Kraul to lead the attacks, the caster Nak, the tracker Kuz and their warrior leader Lok Orcbane, far to the south. When their skulls were brought to him, Mangletooth regretted nothing. Lok's was carried to Thork, who had never imagined who his true foe was.

title: The Samophlange
body: Sputtervalve of the Tinkers' Union, already in hot water over his shredder program, learned that the Venture Company was experimenting with something called a samophlange at a small research site southwest of the Sludge Fen. No one could say what a samophlange was, which only made him want it more. With a copy of the site's operating manual in hand, the console could be mastered: three valves shut, a key taken from Tinkerer Sniggles, and the samophlange tugged free from a jumble of wires that seemed to serve no purpose. Sputtervalve meant to send it straight to the Union's headquarters in Undermine, but first he had a little look himself, and broke it. For the Horde the device's travels went on. Wenikee Boltbucket, a tinkerer camped south of Mor'shan, added gauges and found its integrity at an all time low. Rilli Greasygob of Orgrimmar, once of the Venture Company, needed the manual hoarded by his old rival Boss Copperplug of the Boulder Lode Mine. If he ever fixes it, he has promised to say what it does.

title: Deep Cover
body: For a year the Shattered Hand worked to plant an agent deep inside the Venture Company, and at last word came from him: the goblins were planning something on a grand scale. Shenthul sent a trusted rogue north of the Sludge Fen to the company's tower, with a flare gun and strict instructions. Two flares, then the Shattered Salute, for Taskmaster Fizzule would kill anyone he did not recognize. The tower's crew had already been weakened by poison. The rogue stole the tower key from Foreman Silixiz, cut down drones, patrollers and lookouts, assassinated Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix and took his head, then picked his lockbox for a cache of Zanzil's altered mixture. Shenthul received both in Orgrimmar and spoke of poor Fizzule, one of the Hand's best, as the price field agents pay.
